description: Stop checking one monitor without deleting it: its status becomes PAUSED and an open incident on it closes without a recovery alert. Use it when the user wants a monitor off for an open-ended time. For a planned deploy or reboot prefer create_maintenance_window, which keeps checking but silences alerts; for many monitors use bulk_pause_monitors; to restart checks use resume_monitor. Requires a key with the write scope. Pausing a paused monitor changes nothing. Returns the monitor in the get_monitor shape.

monitor_id.description: The monitor's uuid from list_monitors. An id that is not a monitor of this organization, or a deleted one, is a 404.

name: pause_monitor

channel_ids.description: Bound notification channels. Empty means every working channel of the organization is alerted.

checked_at.description: Last lookup attempt; null before the first one.

days_left.description: Whole days until expires_at, negative once passed, computed from expires_at whatever the status; null without a date.

domain.description: Registrable domain the expiry belongs to (A-label), e.g. example.com.

expires_at.description: Registration expiry date from the registry; kept from the last answer when a lookup fails.

status.description: PENDING: not looked up yet. OK: the registry gave an expiry date. LAPSED: the registry lists the domain in its redemption or pending-delete period. NO_EXPIRY_DATA: the registry answers without an expiry date. UNSUPPORTED_TLD: the registry publishes no RDAP data. NOT_FOUND: the registry has no such domain. LOOKUP_FAILED: lookups keep failing (over a week since the last answer, or three failures in a row for a domain never looked up); expires_at is the last date seen, null if none. ON_HOLD: the registry lists the domain on hold (client or server hold), so it does not resolve; expires_at is the registry's date. Date alerts (30, 14 and 7 days before expires_at, then expired) come from OK, LAPSED and ON_HOLD. ON_HOLD itself alerts, and NOT_FOUND does on a domain the registry listed before, once two lookups at least a day apart agree. Known values: PENDING, OK, LAPSED, NO_EXPIRY_DATA, UNSUPPORTED_TLD, NOT_FOUND, LOOKUP_FAILED, ON_HOLD.

region_statuses.description:
Per-region latest status, sorted by region name.

Built from ``region_snapshots``; ``job_id`` is dropped (internal
dedup key) and malformed/partial snapshot rows are skipped rather
than failing the read.

status.description: Known values: UP, DEGRADED, DOWN, ERROR.

lifetime_days.description:
Certificate validity (not_after minus not_before) in days, 2 decimals.

Null when either timestamp is missing, unparsable or offset-less.

renewal_expected_by.description:
When a renewal is expected (two thirds of the lifetime).

Set only for short-lived certificates; null for long-lived ones or
when the lifetime is unknown.

status.description: Known values: PENDING, UP, DEGRADED, DOWN, PAUSED.

type.description: Known values: HTTP, PING, SSL, TCP, DNS.

title: Pause a monitor
